citations.quote: A native programming language for humans and LLMs — less ceremony, less ambiguity, maximum meaning per token.

general_context.limitations_of_proxies_used: GitHub star/fork counts and release counts are used only as declared, consistently-collected supplementary signals alongside the qualitative package-population evidence, per the methodology's restriction against using raw popularity indicators as a standalone proxy.
general_context.subject_identity: Quidra is a real (recently created) open-source project at github.com/quidra-lang/quidra, described as a statically typed native language for humans and LLMs, distinct from the fictional-sounding internal spec docs which describe an actual implemented compiler/runtime.

findings: Core repo quidra-lang/quidra has 4 tagged releases (v0.1.0, v0.2.0, v0.3.0, v0.3.1) all within a 4-day window (Sep 16-20, 2026).
quidra-lang/dnn has 2 tagged releases (v0.1.0, v0.2.0) within the same short window, each declaring an explicit requires.quidra compatibility range against a specific core release tag.
quidra-lang/vision similarly released v0.1.0 targeting the same core release tag with an explicit requires.quidra range.
The core repo runs first-party package compatibility CI so that core changes are continuously validated against dnn and vision.

All three repositories (quidra, dnn, vision) show 0 GitHub stars and 0 forks, and the dnn repository's own release notes list koba-jon as making 'their first contribution' -- i.e. a single-contributor project with no external community activity observed.

predeclared_sampling.retrieval_route: web_search (provider gateway) against github.com repository/release/PR pages, snapshot time 2026-09-22
predeclared_sampling.selection_rule: For the same frozen population of 2 packages (quidra-dnn, vision) plus the core `quidra` repository itself, record release cadence, contributor count, and community engagement signals (stars/forks) as declared consistent proxies, with their limitations noted per Section on raw popularity indicators.

metric.package_ecosystem_activity_mainte.score_rationale: There is genuine, disciplined recent maintenance activity (multiple semantic-versioned releases, explicit cross-package compatibility ranges, dedicated compatibility CI, atomic release-tag discipline matching docs/development.md) which prevents a score of zero. However the entire visible ecosystem is a single-contributor effort with zero external stars/forks/contributors and only 2 downstream packages total, so this is scored low to reflect genuine but extremely narrow, unproven, single-maintainer maintenance activity rather than a broad actively-maintained package ecosystem.

citations.quote: vision is Quidra's first-party tensor image-processing package.
dnn is Quidra's first-party deep-neural-network package.
Continuously test the released vision and dnn packages against Quidra changes before they land in develop/main, so core changes cannot silently break first-party packages.

findings: Only two packages exist in the entire discoverable Quidra ecosystem: quidra-dnn and vision.
Both packages are authored by the same single core-team contributor as the compiler itself (koba-jon), not by an independent third party.
No independent/community (non quidra-lang org) package repository was found for any domain via targeted search.
docs/packages.md documents the install mechanism itself (`quidra install owner/repository`) but the only concretely named distributions anywhere in the docs are the two first-party ones.

predeclared_sampling.candidate_universe: docs/packages.md and docs/spec/language.md name exactly two first-party distributions: `quidra-dnn` (resolves to github.com/quidra-lang/dnn) and the vision package (github.com/quidra-lang/vision). No package registry/index exists (installation is by exact Git release tag only), so the candidate universe was cross-checked with web search for any independent (non quidra-lang org) repository declaring a `quidra.package` / `requires.quidra` manifest.
domain_checklist: CLI argument-parsing framework (beyond built-in cli block)
async task-queue or actor concurrency framework
queries_used: quidra-lang dnn github stars forks contributors
predeclared_sampling.selection_rule: Freeze the complete, deterministic population of Quidra packages discoverable through the language's own documented installation contract (docs/packages.md / docs/spec/language.md 'Package management'), i.e. every distribution reachable via `quidra install <name>` under the official `quidra-` namespace, plus any independently discoverable third-party `owner/repository` package referenced from the same docs or found via targeted web search for 'quidra' package repositories outside the quidra-lang GitHub organization.

metric.third_party_library_availability_.score_rationale: Only 2 of 12 predeclared common ecosystem domains have any installable Quidra package at all, and even those two are first-party (single core maintainer) rather than genuinely independent third-party libraries; no package registry, discovery index, or community-authored package was found for any domain (web, database, testing, serialization, CLI, logging, GUI, concurrency, crypto, regex). This is treated as low-but-nonzero real evidence per Section 26 (absent coverage in a metric intentionally testing it is scored low, not N/A).
